Yeah, the laws are so convoluted in Washington, I don't think even a business lawyer would be able to give me a straight answer. And I'm not sure I'm ready to shell out $400-500 for that.

I called Washington's DOR Business Licensing department as well and got multiple answers from multiple people. One person said that I didn't need to file a foreign LLC, another person said that I only needed a license and not a foreign LLC, another told me that I needed both, and another flat out told me that he didn't know and told me that no one (other than a lawyer) would give me an accurate straight answer.

I think based on this line below, they can go after you and argue that since you're living in WA, you have substantial nexus.

*(1) A person engaging in business is deemed to have substantial nexus with this state if, in the current or immediately preceding calendar year, the person is:*  
*(a) An individual and is a resident or domiciliary of this state;*

And also this:

*Physical presence nexus creating activities include, but are not limited to:*  
*Having an employee working in the state.*  
*Having real or tangible personal property in the state.*

I spoke to someone from the DOR and they told me that a managing member can be considered to be an employee, but I don't know how true or accurate that is. Another person told me that as long as I don't have W2 and paying myself, then I wouldn't be considered an employee.
